rounds.text: ABS Marine Services is significantly undervalued relative to its peers, trading at a P/E of 4.59x and an EV/EBITDA of 4.56x against sector benchmarks of 18.65x and 10.55x, respectively [E6, E11]. This valuation gap persists despite explosive trailing twelve-month profit growth of 191% and a robust return on equity of 29.84%, which dwarfs the sector average of 4.86% [E19, E9]. The company’s operational efficiency is underscored by a cash conversion ratio of 2.07x and a sharp reduction in working capital requirements from 45.2 days to 21.7 days [E27, E54]. Consequently, discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 1344 per share, providing a 76.9% margin of safety from the current price [E39, E40]. Management expects to maintain high EBITDA margins between 45% and 50% while expanding the fleet by seven to eight vessels to capitalize on strong demand, including an upcoming 20-vessel tender from ONGC [E70, E72, E88]. Conceded: the company currently pays no dividends [E4], maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x [E31], and carries contingent liabilities of Rs 310 Cr [E57]. Nevertheless, the stock maintains a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, signaling that the market is beginning to recognize this fundamental outperformance [E45, E51].

The company's financial stability is pressured by a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x [E31], following a surge in borrowings to Rs 377 Cr [E33] that has left free cash flow at a negative Rs -187 Cr [E29]. This aggressive leverage coincides with a massive exit by domestic institutions, who slashed their holdings from 10.03% to a negligible 0.43% [E37], resulting in overall negative institutional money flow [E38] [E63]. Investors face significant risks from contingent liabilities totaling Rs 310 Cr [E57]—nearly 40% of the total market capitalization [E3]—alongside high annualized volatility of 60.1% [E48]. Operational risks are inherent in the company's cyclical earnings profile [E52], where monsoon seasons force a halt in work for offshore contractors due to safety risks [E86]. Furthermore, management's forward guidance suggests a sharp deceleration, with top-line growth expected at only 10% [E69] compared to the trailing twelve-month sales growth of 77% [E16]. Conceded: the company currently reports a strong return on equity of 29.84% [E9] and an attractive P/E ratio of 9.67 [E1] relative to its sector [E6].

While borrowings have risen to Rs 377 Cr [E33] and free cash flow is negative [E29], these figures reflect a strategic $15 million investment in new vessels [E76] supported by an operating cash flow that is 115% of operating profit [E30] and profits fully backed by cash [E27]. Conceded: domestic institutions have reduced their holdings [E37] and the company faces contingent liabilities [E57], yet promoters have increased their stake to 63.96% [E35] and lenders remain comfortable with the current leverage [E83]. Although the business is cyclical [E52] and monsoon-affected [E86], demand remains robust with a pending 20-vessel tender from ONGC [E72] and rising offshore investments globally [E73]. The bear's concern over a 10% top-line guidance [E69] overlooks that management expects to maintain high EBITDA margins between 45% and 50% [E70] while expanding the fleet by seven to eight vessels over a two to three year period [E88]. Furthermore, the current market price of Rs 310 [E2] offers a 76.9% margin of safety [E40] against an intrinsic value of Rs 1344 [E39], suggesting the market is pricing in a -2.3% earnings contraction [E41] despite a five-year profit CAGR of 123% [E17]. Conceded: the stock experiences high annualized volatility of 60.1% [E48].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 168 Cr and stands at 115% of operating profit [E28, E30]. However, the bull's dismissal of financial risk ignores that borrowings doubled from Rs 178 Cr to Rs 377 Cr in a single year [E33], pushing debt-to-equity to 1.21x where debt exceeds net worth [E31], alongside a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -187 Cr [E29]. Conceded: promoters increased their stake slightly to 63.96% [E35]. Nevertheless, institutional confidence has collapsed as domestic institutions slashed holdings from 10.03% to 0.43% [E37] and foreign institutions trimmed stakes [E36], creating a negative money flow signal [E38]. The bull points to robust demand from tenders [E72], but management explicitly admits that offshore contractors halt work during the monsoon due to safety risks [E86], and volatile foreign exchange rates have pushed vessel acquisition costs higher up to Rs 96 per dollar [E85]. Finally, while the bull leans on high past profit growth [E17], the yearly operating margin trend reads inconsistent over the last two years [E25] and the stock carries an alarming 60.1% annualized volatility with a steep historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -77.2% [E47, E48].

Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 377 Cr, pushing debt-to-equity to 1.21x [E31, E33], and free cash flow reached Rs -187 Cr [E29]. However, this heavy capital expenditure directly funded fleet expansion—including the successful induction of the Artemis and upcoming OSV delivery—backed by a massive operating cash flow of Rs 168 Cr that fully covers operating profit at 115% [E28, E30, E74, E75]. Conceded: domestic institutions reduced holdings significantly [E37], yet promoter confidence remains steadfast with an increased stake of 63.96% [E35]. While the bear highlights monsoon work stoppages [E86] and foreign exchange fluctuations affecting acquisition costs [E85], management's robust guidance points to a 10% top-line increase and EBITDA margins sustained between 45% and 50% [E69, E70], supported by strong baseline demand from ONGC's 20-vessel tender [E72]. Conceded: annualized volatility sits at 60.1% [E48], but the company's operating margin has expanded sharply to 47.28% in FY26 [E77] alongside a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 191% [E19], completely overshadowing historical drawdown concerns with concrete operational outperformance.

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 168 Cr and operating profit is fully backed at 115% [E28, E30]. However, that operating influx was completely swallowed by asset outlays, resulting in a severe negative free cash flow of Rs -187 Cr [E29] driven by borrowings climbing sharply to Rs 377 Cr and pushing debt-to-equity to an aggressive 1.21x [E31, E33]. Conceded: promoter confidence grew slightly by 0.54 percentage points [E35], but domestic institutions fled the counter by dumping 9.60 percentage points of their stake [E37], creating a negative institutional money flow signal [E38]. The bull points to management's 10% top-line guidance and 45% to 50% EBITDA margins [E69, E70], but ignores that these forward-looking statements are explicitly acknowledged by management to carry unpredictable known and unknown risks [E87]. Finally, while the bull minimizes operational hazards, management explicitly warned that offshore EPC contractors must halt operations during monsoons due to severe life safety risks [E86], and foreign exchange costs have escalated significantly from Rs 82 to Rs 96 per dollar [E85].

evidence.quote: As regards the guidance on the top line is concerned, we can expect a 10% increase -- assuming that all the vessels will be running in the second half.

evidence.fact: Management expects EBITDA margins to continue in the 45% to 50% band.
evidence.quote: As regards the EBITDA is concerned, I am sure that currently it is in the band of 45 to 50. I am sure that that will continue.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the demand for oil drilling and production programs requires vessels, keeping demand strong.
evidence.quote: So, looking at that, we feel that the demand for all these kind of any oil drilling program or production program, you need vessels. And that is where we come in. So, we hope that the demand will be always there quite strong.

evidence.fact: Management noted that ONGC has a pending tender for about 20 vessels.
evidence.quote: See, demand is as of -- as we talk now, ONGC is asking for about 20-vessel tender is going to come.

evidence.fact: Offshore investments are rising steadily across continents.
evidence.quote: Offshore investments are rising steadily across continents

evidence.fact: Management successfully inducted the offshore support vessel Artemis into the owned fleet during H2 FY26.
evidence.quote: As part of this strategy, during H2 FY26, we successfully inducted the offshore support vessel, Artemis, into our owned fleet, expanding our vessel ownership portfolio and improving our ability to participate in higher-value offshore projects.

evidence.fact: Management is scheduled to take delivery of an offshore supply vessel in Q1 FY27.
evidence.quote: Further enhancing our offshore capabilities, we are also scheduled to take delivery of an offshore supply vessel in Q1 FY27.

evidence.fact: Management stated that approximately $15 million was spent for both new vessels.
evidence.quote: Just a moment. We have totally, we have spent about $15 million for both the vessels.

evidence.fact: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded sharply by 1,763 basis points to 47.28% in FY26.
evidence.quote: EBITDA increased significantly by 179.17% to INR152.55 crores, while the EBITDA margin expanded sharply by 1,763 basis points to 47.28%.

evidence.fact: Management estimated the idle vessel cost at approximately $1,700 a day.
evidence.quote: So, let's put it as a ballpoint figure, it's about $1,700 a day.

evidence.fact: Management stated that fuel efficiency provides a huge advantage as fuel prices have increased.
evidence.quote: That is true because we have this huge advantage in fuel.

evidence.fact: Management operates a diversified fleet supported by over 2,000 seafarers and shore-based professionals.
evidence.quote: Today, we operate a diversified fleet with offices in Mumbai, Kochi, Singapore, and Kakinada, supported by over 2,000 seafarers and shore-based professionals.

evidence.fact: Management stated that out of eight owned vessels, five are on long-term charter, two have just come out of charter, and a third newly acquired vessel goes into dry dock.
evidence.quote: Out of the eight vessels that we own, five of them are on long-term charter, three of them -- two of them have just come out of charter, and third one is just we have acquired, so it has to go into the dry dock and then only come out and then only we put her in the market.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the total fleet stands at 12 vessels including four smaller vessels on long-term charter.
evidence.quote: No, 12 number is correct. The other four vessels are smaller vessels, they are on long-term charter.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the debt-equity ratio is comfortable for lenders.
evidence.quote: At this point of time with our debt-equity ratio the banks are also comfortable. I don't think we have overshot on the debt side.

evidence.fact: Management explained that tonnage tax is calculated based on vessel tonnage rather than earnings.
evidence.quote: So, what they do is they tax not as per the earnings, they tax on the tonnage of the vessel.

evidence.fact: Management noted that exchange rate fluctuations impact vessel acquisition costs.
evidence.quote: The premium is only because of the exchange rate. Other than that, I don't see much change in this because from what we were paying INR82 per dollar, it has gone up to INR96.

evidence.fact: Management stated that offshore EPC contractors avoid working during the monsoon season due to safety risks.
evidence.quote: During the monsoon, they cannot work. Considering risk of there was a huge loss of life and all that, so they are very careful that they should not work with during the monsoon time.

evidence.fact: Management noted that forward-looking statements are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and assumptions that are difficult to predict.
evidence.quote: Such forward-looking statements are not guarantee of future performance and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and assumptions that are difficult to predict.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): Management expects to expand the fleet by adding seven to eight vessels over a period of two to three years.
evidence.quote: I think Captain has already told that the vision is to expand and to go forward for seven to eight vessels over a period of two to three years.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (H2 FY26): Management stated that the second year operation with Schlumberger is underway for AM Passion.
evidence.quote: And now we are on the second year operation with them.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY28): Management stated that charter rates for AM Passion will increase to $19,000 in the third year.
evidence.quote: And then the next three years, it will be at $19,000.

evidence.quote: We stay committed to building a robust asset base that drives operational efficiency, enhances service delivery, and supports sustainable long-term growth.
